a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

Eluxadoline, which shares the query's high ionization/zwitterionic character, has measured human oral bioavailability of about 1%, far below 20%.
DMT, a simple tryptamine, has estimated absolute oral bioavailability of about 10-15%, below 20%.
Agomelatine, another low-bioavailability CNS-type molecule, has absolute oral bioavailability below 5%.
The query combines the indole-ethylamine scaffold of sumatriptan/DMT with the ionization liability of eluxadoline; no high-F context with comparable structure is transferable.

Hydroxamic acid metabolic fate (glucuronidation, reduction) and its effect on first-pass extraction are unmeasured.
Species differences (e.g., sumatriptan dog 58%, toceranib dog 77%) limit cross-species transfer; the endpoint is human oral bioavailability.
The low neutral fraction is a permeability liability, but actual transporter/efflux effects are unknown.
